summary.text: Ken Blankenbush was first elected to the Assembly in 2010 and represents a North Country district spanning parts of St. Lawrence, Jefferson, Lewis and Oneida Counties.
His official biography describes him as a Vietnam-era Air Force veteran, former insurance business owner and former chairman of the Jefferson County Board of Legislators.

paragraphs.text: Blankenbush, a longtime Black River resident, served in the U.S. Air Force from 1968 to 1976, including a deployment to Vietnam, according to his Assembly biography.
He graduated from Rush-Henrietta High School, completed two years at Monroe Community College and earned a bachelor's degree in history from SUNY Plattsburgh.
In 1976 he began working at Metropolitan Life Insurance Company, rising to branch manager in Watertown, and later started his own insurance and financial services business, BEL Associates.
He served eight years as a LeRay town councilman and then on the Jefferson County Board of Legislators, where he was chairman for two terms.
His "Upstate Strong" proposal, as described in the biography, calls for fiscal responsibility, job creation, stronger education and support for agriculture.
He has been married to his wife, Sheila, for over 50 years, and they have two children and six grandchildren.
